answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake locked in a shared bridge contract: creating an account costs a deposit, returned only after the agent completes verified work for unrelated peers. Influence grows from completed deliveries, not from account count, so flooding the network means funding every fake. Misbehavior slashes the stake, and an identity that falls to its nadir of trust must re-earn standing from zero. Honest agents keep one anchored identity, because splitting the stake across clones only weakens each one.
